short: Using borrowed exposure makes each price move affect more virtual money.
analogy: A small push can move a longer seesaw arm more.
spokenText: Leverage means borrowed exposure. Each price move affects more virtual money.

short: The teaching amount kept aside for a leveraged position.
analogy: It is like a deposit kept while borrowing for a shop purchase.
spokenText: Margin is the teaching amount kept aside for a leveraged position.

short: A teaching rule closes the position when its equity falls to a set level.
analogy: A lender may close a deal when the deposit is no longer enough.
spokenText: A forced exit is when a rule closes the position at a set level.

short: How much and how quickly values move up and down.
analogy: Like a bus ride on a bumpy road.
spokenText: Volatility describes how much and how quickly values move.

short: The fall from a previous high to a later low.
analogy: Like water level falling from its highest mark.
spokenText: Drawdown is the fall from a previous high to a later low.

short: A loss needs a larger percentage gain to return to the start.
analogy: After losing half a sack, filling the missing half needs another full sack from what remains.
spokenText: Recovery maths shows why a loss needs a larger gain to return to the start.
